title: Governor Abbott directs TCEQ to halt data center permits pending ERCOT audit
text:
← Back to the wire
State Government
Governor Abbott directs TCEQ to halt data center permits pending ERCOT audit
Governor Greg Abbott has ordered a pause on new permits for data centers in Texas until key audits are completed regarding electric grid reliability and resource use. The move requires multiple agencies’ cooperation before further approvals can proceed. Data center projects may face new regulations following upcoming legislative sessions.
Governor Greg Abbott directed the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to halt all permits sought by data centers until the Electric Reliability Council of Texas completes its audit, according to a Sept. 21 announcement. The directive states that no state agency shall move forward with regulatory approvals related to data center development until necessary information is acquired for informed decisions by the Public Utility Commission of Texas, ERCOT, and the Texas Water Development Board.
"Simply put, Texans must come first," said Governor Abbott. "Data centers must pay their own way, protect our grid and water, and complete the ERCOT and TWDB audits. Until they do, TCEQ will issue no permits sought by data center projects."
Abbott instructed the Public Utility Commission and ERCOT to audit all data centers undergoing ERCOT’s interconnection process in order to ensure that their development does not compromise grid reliability or put natural resources at risk. On September 14, he directed the Texas Water Development Board to require compliance with water-use reporting requirements from data centers, impose legal consequences for failure to comply with state law, and partner with ERCOT on obtaining additional water-use information through audits.
The statement outlines that data center projects must cover all electrical infrastructure costs, result in lower residential electrical bills, complete required audits by ERCOT, avoid using water needed by local communities, report electricity and water usage accurately, and adhere to setback requirements intended for community protection.
As these audits proceed at ERCOT and TWDB, TCEQ is required to align its permitting decisions with these directives. The commission must provide an update on compliance with this directive to the Office of the Governor by Monday, October 19.
Looking ahead to next session, Abbott said he will work with lawmakers "to eliminate any financial incentives for data centers." Greg Abbott serves as the 48th governor leading the office which provides services across Texas; it also advances cultural understanding through commissions supporting opportunities for women and people with disabilities while promoting economic opportunity and public safety in line with state values. Additionally, it operates from a historic mansion dating back to 1856 that stands as one of America’s oldest continuously occupied governor's residences,according to the official website.
